mechanism_narrative: A sustained 5-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above its 12-month moving average signals rising consumer demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth above trend is not followed by a statistically significant increase in S&P 500 returns (p < 0.05) in at least 60% of historical instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average signals weakening manufacturing output, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines are not followed by negative S&P 500 returns in at least 70% of historical cases, or if the correlation coefficient falls below 0.4, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% triggers a tightening cycle that increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as equity valuations adjust downward.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of subsequent 60-day periods, or if the Rank IC exceeds 0.05, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% signals labor market weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises above 6.5% but S&P 500 returns are not negative in at least 60% of historical cases, or if the correlation coefficient is below 0.3, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month increase in the real sales of domestic product (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average signals rising aggregate demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth above trend is not followed by a statistically significant increase in S&P 500 returns (p < 0.05) in at least 60% of historical instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below its 6-month moving average signals weakening residential construction activity, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as housing sector earnings decline.
failure_condition: If HOUST declines are not followed by negative S&P 500 returns in at least 70% of historical cases, or if the correlation coefficient falls below 0.4, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.5% signals inflationary pressures, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as equity valuations adjust downward due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL rises above 3.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of subsequent 60-day periods, or if the Rank IC exceeds 0.05, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the employment-population ratio (UNRATE) above 60% signals labor market strength, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises above 60% but S&P 500 returns are not positive in at least 60% of historical cases, or if the correlation coefficient is below 0.3, the hypothesis is falsified.
